docs.title: PyHive
docs.text:
PyHive is the Python SDK and command-line tool for the Hive learning management system. It reads and changes programs, subjects, modules, exercises, assignments, users, classes, the schedule and help requests.

  • pyhive — a CLI for quick reads and deletes, with --json output for scripts and agents. → CLI reference
  • from pyhive import HiveClient — a typed Python client for everything else. → Python SDK
  • Examples — runnable scripts shipped in the package. → Examples
  • Claude Code skill — teaches an agent to use both. → Agent skill

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install PyHiveLMS --index-url https://system-b90.github.io/.github/pypi/
pyhive version

Each release is published to both PyPI (pip install PyHiveLMS) and the System-B90 package index above. Python 3.10 or newer.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
pyhive auth login                   # pick the server and sign in once through the browser
pyhive programs list
pyhive --json subjects list | jq '.subjects[].name'
pyhive examples run program_tree

from pyhive import HiveClient

with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org") as client:
    program = next(iter(client.get_programs()))
    for subject in program.get_subjects():
        modules = list(subject.get_modules())
        print(f"[{subject.symbol}] {subject.name}: {len(modules)} modules")

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text:
The pages here double as a Claude Code skill called pyhive. Install it one of two ways:

# From the installed package, into ~/.claude/skills/pyhive:
pyhive docs install-skill

# Or as a plugin, which also installs PyHive when it is missing:
claude plugin marketplace add System-B90/.github
claude plugin install pyhive@system-b90-marketplace

Without Claude Code, point an agent at pyhive docs show skill: it prints the same guide.

docs.title: The docs in your terminal
docs.text:
Every page here ships inside the package:

pyhive docs                 # list the pages
pyhive docs show sdk        # print one as Markdown

The published site is built from those same files, so the site, the terminal and the skill always match the installed version.

docs.title: Supported Hive versions
docs.text: PyHive works with the exact Hive releases it has been verified against. pyhive versions lists them. Connecting to any other release raises UnverifiedHiveVersionError; upgrade PyHive, or see Versions.

docs.title: PyHive for agents
docs.text:
pyhive is a Typer CLI over the PyHive SDK (pip package PyHiveLMS, import name pyhive). This page is self-contained for everyday work. Do not read the PyHive source to use it.

Need Read Every command, option and output shape cli.md · pyhive docs show cli Writing a Python script against Hive sdk.md · pyhive docs show sdk A working script to start from examples.md · pyhive examples list

docs.title: CLI or SDK?
docs.text:
The CLI covers list / get / delete for programs, subjects, modules, exercises, assignments, classes and users, plus creating staff users. Anything else — filtering, creating course content or students, the schedule, help requests, bulk changes, joins across resources — is a short SDK script. Run it inline:

python - <<'EOF'
from pyhive.cli.client_factory import default_hive_url, get_hive_client
client = get_hive_client(default_hive_url(), verify=False)  # same server and sign-in as the CLI
for module in client.get_modules(parent_subject__id=12):
    print(module.id, module.order, module.name)
EOF

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
pyhive version            # installed? prints the PyHive version
pip install PyHiveLMS --index-url https://system-b90.github.io/.github/pypi/   # if not

docs.title: Signing in without a browser
docs.text:
With no credentials, every command falls back to SSO, which opens a browser and blocks until someone signs in. An agent must supply credentials. The CLI tries, in order:

  1. -u USER -p PASS (root options)
  2. -t TOKEN / --token TOKEN (root option); a personal access token (hive_pat_...) or an API token
  3. the HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable (same kinds)
  4. the OS keyring cache from pyhive auth login (or --cache-token), used only for the server it was saved for
  5. SSO in the browser

Check first with pyhive --json auth status: {"hive_url": ..., "token_cached": true} means commands already sign in silently to that server. Otherwise ask the user to run this once in their own terminal (in Claude Code: ! pyhive auth login). It asks for the Hive URL, signs in through the browser, and stores the URL and both tokens in the OS keyring. Every later pyhive call, and get_hive_client(default_hive_url(), ...) in scripts, then uses that server, signs in silently and refreshes the token itself. Never run auth login yourself: it prompts, then blocks on the browser.

With no browser (CI, a remote box), use a Hive personal access token: the user creates one in Hive (account menu, Access Tokens; read only is enough for reading) and puts it in HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN, or stores it once with pyhive auth login --token hive_pat_... --hive-url URL. A PAT is never refreshed. When Hive refuses one, the error says why: an expired token's message names its expiry date, and a read-only token's 403 names the refused method. Never print or log a token.

Scripts reuse the same chain through get_hive_client() (as in the snippet above), so they need no credentials of their own.

docs.title: Rules for calling the CLI
docs.text:
• Always pass --json. stdout then holds one JSON document; progress lines (Fetching …) are suppressed.
  • --json, -u, -p, -t, --hive-url, --verify and --cache-token work anywhere on the line. One exception: in users create, --password is the new account's password, so a sign-in password goes before users (pyhive -p PW users create ...).
  • A --hive-url other than the cached server skips the cached token and falls back to SSO, so leave it out unless the user names another server.
  • Defaults: the server cached by auth login, else https://hive.org; TLS verification off.
  • Exit code 0 on success, 1 on any error. In --json mode the error is JSON on stderr: {"error": "...", "details": "..."}.
  • delete commands do not prompt. Confirm with the user before running one. Deleting a subject also deletes its modules and exercises.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
pyhive --json programs list                 # {"programs": [...]}
pyhive --json programs get 2                # {"program": {...}}
pyhive --json programs delete 2             # {"deleted_program_id": 2, "status": "success"}
# Same list/get/delete for: subjects, modules, exercises, classes, queues
pyhive --json queues items QID | add-item QID --exercise ID|--nested-queue ID|--module ID [--order N --rule R --disabled]
pyhive --json queues update-item QID ITEM [--rule R --enabled/--disabled] | move-item QID ITEM POS | expand-item QID ITEM | remove-item QID ITEM
pyhive --json queues create NAME --module ID|--user ID | update QID [--name --description] | duplicate QID NAME
pyhive --json users set-queues UID [--queue ID|none --user-queue ID|none --override-queue ID|none --disable-queue/--enable-queue]
pyhive --json classes set-queue CID QID|none | set-lesson CID LESSON|none | clear-override-queues CID
pyhive --json lessons list [--module ID]    # lesson ids: UUIDs on Hive 7.3+
pyhive --json assignments list | get ID     # no delete
pyhive --json users list | delete ID        # no get
pyhive --json users create USERNAME --password PW --clearance checker --gender female \
    [--first-name --last-name --number --status --teacher/--no-teacher --confirmed/--no-confirmed]

pyhive --json auth status                   # {"hive_url", "token_cached", "token_type", "env_token_set"}; no network
pyhive auth login | logout                  # user runs login (prompts + browser); logout clears the cache
pyhive --json token [--cache-token]         # SSO in the browser → {"access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_at"}
pyhive --json register NAME REDIRECT_URI    # register an SSO client app → client_id/secret
pyhive --json version | versions            # PyHive version / Hive versions it supports

pyhive docs [show PAGE | path | install-skill]
pyhive examples [list | show NAME | run NAME [ARGS...]]

list and get return every field Hive sends, under Hive's wire names: related objects are plain ids under program, checker, mentor, parent_subject, parent_module, user, exercise, and classes/users are id lists. The SDK names the same fields program_id, mentor_id, class_ids and so on.

Enum names accepted by users create (any case): --clearance HANICH (student) · CHECKER · SEGEL (staff) · ADMIN; --gender MALE · FEMALE · NONBINARY; --status defaults to PRESENT. users create cannot make a student — a student needs a program and a number, and the command has no --program. Use client.create_student(...) in the SDK.

Parse output with jq or Python:

pyhive --json subjects list | jq -r '.subjects[] | "\(.id)\t\(.symbol)\t\(.name)"'
pyhive --json users list | python -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)['users']))"

docs.title: SDK essentials
docs.text:
from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import AssignmentStatusEnum, ClearanceEnum

with HiveClient("admin", "password", "https://hive.org", verify=False) as client:
    program = client.get_program(2)
    for subject in program.get_subjects():          # list endpoints return generators
        for module in subject.get_modules():
            print(subject.symbol, module.order, module.name)

    student = client.get_student(number=1234)        # or name="First Last"; None if no single match
    done = [a for a in client.get_assignments(for_user=student)
            if a.assignment_status == AssignmentStatusEnum.DONE]
  • List methods (get_*s) return generators: wrap in list(...) to index, count or reuse them.
  • Methods accept an id or a model wherever they take a related object (get_assignments(for_user=student) or for_user=13).
  • Relations on models (assignment.user, user.mentor, class_.users) are lazy and cost one request each. In loops, fetch the table once ({u.id: u for u in client.get_users()}) and join by id.
  • Enums live in pyhive.types; compare with members, not strings.
  • *_name= filters (subject_name=, module_name=, …) are exact matches. Passing two filters that contradict each other raises AssertionError.
  • Errors: HTTP 400 → ValueError("HTTP 400 Error: {...}") with Hive's message; other HTTP errors → httpx.HTTPStatusError; a failed delete → RuntimeError; an unlisted Hive version → UnverifiedHiveVersionError (pass skip_version_check=True to try anyway).

Full method reference and recipes: sdk.md.

docs.title: Known quirks
docs.text:
• Queues: a queue has exactly one owner (--module or --user). Item positions are 0-based and change only through move-item. Hive rejects nesting a user's own queue in a module queue, duplicating an empty queue, and adding a module that has no exercises. duplicate always keeps the original's owner. classes set-lesson CID none keeps the queues the lesson assigned.
  • get_user_me() raises NotImplementedError.
  • Staff accounts can only open chat help requests (client.create_chat(with_user=…)); create_help_request with another type is rejected with Staff may only create staff chats.
  • get_student(name=…) matches the full name, display name or username first, then the first name alone. It returns None when nothing matches and raises RuntimeError when several users share that first name.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
pyhive is installed with the PyHiveLMS package. It is built on the Python SDK, so anything a command does, a script can do too. The CLI covers the everyday reads and deletes; the SDK covers everything else.

pyhive --help              # command groups
pyhive programs --help     # one group
pyhive docs show cli       # this page, in the terminal

docs.title: Command line shape
docs.text:
pyhive GROUP COMMAND [ARGS] [OPTIONS]

These options work anywhere on the line: before the group, between the group and the command, or after the command. pyhive --json programs list, pyhive programs --json list and pyhive programs list --json are the same.

Option What it does -u, --username Hive username (with -p) -p, --password Hive password (with -u) -t, --token Hive personal access token (hive_pat_...) or API token --json Print one JSON document on stdout instead of text --cache-token Save the server and token in the OS keyring for later calls --hive-url URL Server to talk to. Default: the cached one, else https://hive.org --verify/--no-verify Verify TLS certificates. Default --no-verify

A command's own option comes first

pyhive users create USERNAME --password PW sets the new account's password. To sign in with a password on that command, put -p (or --password) before users. Anything after a bare -- is passed through untouched.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
Sign in once:

pyhive auth login

It asks for the Hive URL (Enter keeps the one shown), opens the browser on Hive's sign-in page, and saves the URL, the access token and the refresh token in the OS keyring (service pyhive_cli). Later commands talk to that server by default, sign in without a browser, and refresh the access token when it expires. Anyone who can read your keyring can act as you, so only do this on your own machine.

pyhive auth login --hive-url https://hive.example   # no prompt
pyhive auth login --token hive_pat_...              # store a personal access token instead (no browser)
pyhive auth status                                  # cached server, and whether (and which kind of) token is cached
pyhive auth logout                                  # forget the server and the tokens

auth status only reads the keyring. It does not check that the token still works.

auth login --token takes a personal access token made in Hive (account menu, Access Tokens). It checks the token against the server, then caches it the same way; it has no refresh token and works until it expires or is revoked. Use this on machines without a browser.

Every command that talks to Hive picks the first credentials it finds:

  1. -u USER -p PASS
  2. -t TOKEN
  3. the HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable
  4. the keyring cache from pyhive auth login or --cache-token, if it was saved for the same server the command talks to
  5. otherwise, SSO: a browser opens on Hive's sign-in page and the command waits for you to finish

--cache-token on any command saves the server it used and the token it ended up with, the same way auth login does. Without --hive-url, commands use the cached server, or https://hive.org if none is cached. Giving --hive-url for a different server ignores the cached token instead of sending it there.

A token from -t or HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN cannot be refreshed. A personal access token (hive_pat_...) lasts until the expiry chosen when it was made, so it is the one to use for scripts and CI; a token from pyhive token expires soon, then get a new one.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Text mode prints progress lines and aligned lists for people. With --json, stdout holds exactly one JSON document:

Command kind JSON on stdout list {"programs": [{...}, ...]} — key is the group name get {"program": {...}} — key is the singular delete {"deleted_program_id": 2, "status": "success"} error nothing on stdout; {"error": "...", "details": "..."} on stderr

The exit code is 0 on success and 1 on any error. Lists are sorted by id.

Objects carry every field Hive returns, under Hive's own field names. Related objects appear as ids: "program": 2, "mentor": 1, "classes": [1, 3]. (The SDK models expose the same values as program_id, mentor_id, class_ids.)

pyhive --json subjects list | jq -r '.subjects[] | "\(.id)\t\(.symbol)\t\(.name)"'
pyhive --json users list | jq '[.users[] | select(.clearance == 1)] | length'   # students

docs.title: Course content
docs.text:
Programs contain subjects, subjects contain modules, modules contain exercises.

pyhive programs list
pyhive programs get 2
pyhive programs delete 2

pyhive subjects list
pyhive subjects get 12
pyhive subjects delete 12        # also deletes the subject's modules and exercises

pyhive modules list
pyhive modules get 40
pyhive modules delete 40

pyhive exercises list
pyhive exercises get 7
pyhive exercises delete 7

Running a group with no command runs its list: pyhive subjects is pyhive subjects list.

Deletes do not ask for confirmation

delete commands run immediately and cannot be undone.

The CLI does not create or edit course content. Use the SDK: program.create_subject(...), subject.create_module(...), module.create_exercise(...) — see the build_module example.

docs.title: Assignments
docs.text:
An assignment is one student's copy of one exercise.

pyhive assignments list
pyhive assignments get 1234

list returns every assignment the account can see. To filter (by student, mentor, module, subject…), use client.get_assignments(...) in the SDK.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
A class is either a room or a student group ("type": "Room" / "Student Group").

pyhive classes list
pyhive classes get 3
pyhive classes delete 3

# Assign to every student in the class:
pyhive classes set-queue 3 12          # class queue 12; `none` clears it
pyhive classes set-lesson 3 6c14e49d-ab72-4675-8279-2aa840d6a95b   # or `none`
pyhive classes clear-override-queues 3 # Hive 6.1.1+

set-lesson applies the lesson's queue rules: each student a rule matches gets that rule's queue as their class queue. Find lesson ids with pyhive lessons list (UUIDs on Hive 7.3+, integers before). Setting the lesson to none keeps the queues it assigned.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
pyhive users list
pyhive users delete 15
pyhive users set-queues 15 --queue 12 --user-queue none --enable-queue
pyhive users create jdoe --password 'S3cret!' --clearance checker --gender female \
    --first-name Jane --last-name Doe

users create options:

Option Values USERNAME required argument --password prompted (hidden) if omitted — always pass it in scripts --clearance required: HANICH (student), CHECKER, SEGEL (staff), ADMIN, any case --gender required: MALE, FEMALE, NONBINARY --status PRESENT (default), RAISED_HAND, TOILET, HOME, MEDICAL, … --number identification number --first-name, --last-name --avatar-filename --teacher/--no-teacher --confirmed/--no-confirmed

On success the JSON is {"user": {...}, "status": "created"}.

Students need the SDK

A student (HANICH) must have a program and a number, and users create has no --program option, so it can only create staff. Create students with client.create_student(username, password, gender, number=..., program=...).

users set-queues sets a student's three queue slots, each to a queue id or none (clears it); a slot you leave out keeps its value:

Option Sets --queue ID\|none the class queue --user-queue ID\|none the student's own queue --override-queue ID\|none the override queue --disable-queue / --enable-queue pauses or resumes the class queue --disable-user-queue / --enable-user-queue pauses or resumes the student's own queue

docs.title: Queues
docs.text:
A queue belongs to exactly one owner: a module (shared) or one user (their own queue). Its items are exercises, nested queues, or a module's exercises, in order from position 0.

pyhive queues list [--user 15 | --module 7 | --class 3] [--user-queues | --module-queues]
pyhive queues get 12
pyhive queues create "Week 3" --module 7        # or --user 15; --description TEXT
pyhive queues update 12 --name "Week 3a" --description "..."
pyhive queues duplicate 12 "Week 3 (copy)"      # same owner, same items
pyhive queues delete 12

pyhive queues items 12                          # the items, in order
pyhive queues add-item 12 --exercise 40         # or --nested-queue 13 / --module 7
pyhive queues add-item 12 --nested-queue 13 --order 0 --rule "wait for done" --disabled
pyhive queues update-item 12 51 --rule choose --enabled --no-continue-on-redo
pyhive queues move-item 12 51 0                 # 0-based; the rest are renumbered
pyhive queues expand-item 12 51                 # replace a nested queue with its items
pyhive queues remove-item 12 51

--rule takes Choose, Wait For Submitted, Wait For AutoChecks or Wait For Done (any case). add-item appends unless --order is given; update-item changes only what you pass and never the position (use move-item). Hive refuses (HTTP 400) to nest a user's own queue in a module queue, to duplicate an empty queue, and to add a module with no exercises.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text: pyhive lessons list [--module 7]        # ids for `classes set-lesson`

docs.title: Sign-in helpers
docs.text:
pyhive token                        # SSO in the browser, prints the access token
pyhive --json token                 # {"access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_at"}
pyhive token --cache-token          # ...and saves the server and both tokens, like `auth login`

pyhive register "My service" http://localhost:5000/api/auth/callback/hive

register creates an SSO (OAuth) client application on Hive and prints its client_id and client_secret, for building another service that signs in with Hive. It needs an account allowed to manage SSO applications.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
pyhive version       # this PyHive's version
pyhive versions      # every Hive release this PyHive is verified against

PyHive checks the server's version when it connects and refuses a Hive release it has not been verified against. Upgrade PyHive when the server is newer; from the SDK, skip_version_check=True tries anyway.

docs.title: Docs and examples
docs.text:
The documentation and example scripts ship inside the package.

pyhive docs list                    # list the pages (also plain `pyhive docs`)
pyhive docs show sdk                # print a page as Markdown
pyhive docs path                    # where the files are
pyhive docs install-skill           # install them as the Claude Code skill `pyhive`
pyhive docs install-skill --project .   # ...into ./.claude/skills instead of ~/.claude/skills

pyhive examples list                # list the example scripts (also plain `pyhive examples`)
pyhive examples show program_tree   # print one
pyhive examples run program_tree 2  # run one against the server

examples run signs in exactly like every other command and passes any extra arguments to the example. Its output is the example's own text, not JSON. python -m pyhive.examples is the same command group.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Runnable scripts ship inside the package. Each one is a short, complete program you can copy as a starting point.

pyhive examples                          # list them
pyhive examples show program_tree        # print one
pyhive examples run program_tree 2       # run one against the server

pyhive examples run signs in the same way as every other pyhive command (see Signing in) and passes extra arguments on to the example. Run as a plain script (python program_tree.py), an example signs in through the browser instead.

Every example defines main(client, *args), so you can also call one from your own code or a notebook:

from pyhive import examples
examples.load("program_tree").main(client, "2")
Example What it does connect Every way to sign in to Hive, then print the server version and what you can see. program_tree Print the course tree — program, subjects, modules, exercises — with counts. find_student Find a student by name or number and show their mentor, classes and progress. assignments_csv Export assignments as CSV — student, subject, module, exercise, status, submissions. class_roster Print every class (rooms and student groups) with its members. weekly_schedule Print the schedule for the next seven days, grouped by day. open_help_requests List open help requests: who asked, about which exercise, and when it was last answered. build_module Create a subject, a module and its exercises from a plain Python outline.

The source of each example is below. (Reading this file raw, as an agent does, the source appears as a --8<-- include line: print it with pyhive examples show NAME.)

docs.title: connect
docs.text:
"""Every way to sign in to Hive, then print the server version and what you can see.

Run:  pyhive examples run connect
"""

import os

from pyhive import HiveClient

HIVE_URL = "https://hive.org"


def connect_with_sso() -> HiveClient:
    # Opens a browser for Hive's SSO page; the token refreshes itself afterwards.
    return HiveClient.from_sso(HIVE_URL, verify=False)


def connect_with_password(username: str, password: str) -> HiveClient:
    return HiveClient(username, password, HIVE_URL, verify=False)


def connect_with_token() -> HiveClient:
    # A bare token cannot be refreshed: once it expires, build a new client.
    # Get one with `pyhive token`.
    return HiveClient.from_api_token(os.environ["HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN"], HIVE_URL)


def main(client: HiveClient, *_args: str) -> None:
    print(f"Hive version: {client.get_hive_version()}")
    print(f"Server time:  {client.get_server_time()}")
    print(f"Programs:     {[program.name for program in client.get_programs()]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with connect_with_sso() as hive:
        main(hive)

docs.title: program_tree
docs.text:
"""Print the course tree — program, subjects, modules, exercises — with counts.

Run:  pyhive examples run program_tree [PROGRAM_ID]
"""

from collections import defaultdict

from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import Exercise, Module


def main(client: HiveClient, *args: str) -> None:
    programs = (
        [client.get_program(int(args[0]))] if args else list(client.get_programs())
    )
    for program in programs:
        # One request per level, grouped locally, instead of one request per
        # subject and per module through subject.get_modules().
        program_filter = [program.id]
        subjects = sorted(client.get_subjects(parent_program__id__in=program_filter))
        modules: dict[int, list[Module]] = defaultdict(list)
        for module in client.get_modules(
            parent_subject__parent_program__id__in=program_filter
        ):
            modules[module.parent_subject_id].append(module)
        exercises: dict[int, list[Exercise]] = defaultdict(list)
        for exercise in client.get_exercises(
            parent_module__parent_subject__parent_program__id__in=program_filter
        ):
            exercises[exercise.parent_module_id].append(exercise)

        print(f"{program.name} (#{program.id})")
        for subject in subjects:
            print(f"  [{subject.symbol}] {subject.name} (#{subject.id})")
            for module in sorted(modules[subject.id], key=lambda m: m.order):
                count = len(exercises[module.id])
                print(f"    {module.order:>3}. {module.name} — {count} exercises")
                for exercise in sorted(exercises[module.id], key=lambda e: e.order):
                    print(f"         - {exercise.name} (#{exercise.id})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive)

docs.title: find_student
docs.text:
"""Find a student by name or number and show their mentor, classes and progress.

Run:  pyhive examples run find_student "First Last"
      pyhive examples run find_student 1234
"""

from collections import Counter

from pyhive import HiveClient


def main(client: HiveClient, *args: str) -> None:
    if not args:
        print("Pass a student name or number. Students:")
        for each in client.get_students():
            print(f"  {each.number}  {each.display_name}")
        return

    query = args[0]
    student = (
        client.get_student(number=int(query))
        if query.isdigit()
        else client.get_student(name=query)
    )
    if student is None:
        print(f"No single student matches {query!r}.")
        return

    print(f"{student.display_name} (#{student.id}, number {student.number})")
    print(f"  status:  {student.status.value if student.status else '-'}")
    print(f"  program: {student.program.name if student.program else '-'}")
    print(f"  mentor:  {student.mentor.display_name if student.mentor else '-'}")
    print(f"  classes: {', '.join(c.name for c in student.classes) or '-'}")

    by_status = Counter(a.assignment_status.value for a in student.get_assignments())
    print("  assignments:")
    for status, count in by_status.most_common():
        print(f"    {status:<18} {count}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive, *sys.argv[1:])

docs.title: assignments_csv
docs.text:
"""Export assignments as CSV — student, subject, module, exercise, status, submissions.

Run:  pyhive examples run assignments_csv > assignments.csv
      pyhive examples run assignments_csv MENTOR_USER_ID   (only that mentor's mentees)
"""

import csv
import sys

from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import Exercise, User


def main(client: HiveClient, *args: str) -> None:
    assignments = (
        client.get_assignments(for_mentees_of=int(args[0]))
        if args
        else client.get_assignments()
    )

    # Fetch each lookup table once. assignment.user / assignment.exercise
    # would issue one request per assignment.
    users: dict[int, User] = {user.id: user for user in client.get_users()}
    exercises: dict[int, Exercise] = {ex.id: ex for ex in client.get_exercises()}

    writer = csv.writer(sys.stdout)
    writer.writerow(
        ["student", "subject", "module", "exercise", "status", "submissions"]
    )
    for assignment in assignments:
        student = users.get(assignment.user_id)
        exercise = exercises.get(assignment.exercise_id)
        writer.writerow(
            [
                student.display_name if student else assignment.user_id,
                exercise.parent_subject_name if exercise else "",
                exercise.parent_module_name if exercise else "",
                exercise.name if exercise else assignment.exercise_id,
                assignment.assignment_status.value,
                assignment.submission_count,
            ]
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive, *sys.argv[1:])

docs.text:
"""Print every class (rooms and student groups) with its members.

Run:  pyhive examples run class_roster
"""

from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import ClassTypeEnum


def main(client: HiveClient, *_args: str) -> None:
    # One users request instead of class.users, which fetches members one by one.
    users = {user.id: user for user in client.get_users()}

    for class_type in ClassTypeEnum:
        print(f"{class_type.value}s")
        for hive_class in client.get_classes(type_=class_type):
            members = [users[uid].display_name for uid in hive_class.user_ids]
            print(f"  {hive_class.name} (#{hive_class.id}) — {len(members)} members")
            for name in sorted(members):
                print(f"      {name}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

        main(hive)

docs.title: weekly_schedule
docs.text:
"""Print the schedule for the next seven days, grouped by day.

Run:  pyhive examples run weekly_schedule
"""

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone

from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import ScheduleEvent


def main(client: HiveClient, *_args: str) -> None:
    start = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(
        hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0
    )
    end = start + timedelta(days=7)

    days: dict[date, list[ScheduleEvent]] = defaultdict(list)
    for event in client.get_schedule_events(start__gte=start, end__lte=end):
        days[event.start.date()].append(event)

    if not days:
        print(f"No events between {start:%Y-%m-%d} and {end:%Y-%m-%d}.")
    for day in sorted(days):
        print(f"{day:%A %Y-%m-%d}")
        for event in sorted(days[day], key=lambda e: e.start):
            category = f" [{event.category_name}]" if event.category_name else ""
            print(f"  {event.start:%H:%M}-{event.end:%H:%M}  {event.title}{category}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive)

docs.text:
"""List open help requests: who asked, about which exercise, and when it was last answered.

Run:  pyhive examples run open_help_requests
"""

from pyhive import HiveClient
from pyhive.types import HelpStatusEnum


def main(client: HiveClient, *_args: str) -> None:
    requests = list(
        client.get_help_requests(
            help_status__in=[HelpStatusEnum.OPEN.value], ordering="-id"
        )
    )
    print(f"{len(requests)} open help requests")
    for request in requests:
        exercise = request.for_exercise
        about = f" — {exercise.name}" if exercise else ""
        print(f"#{request.id} [{request.help_type.value}] {request.title}{about}")
        print(f"    asked by {request.user.display_name}")
        responses = list(client.get_help_responses(request))
        if responses:
            print(
                f"    {len(responses)} replies, last on {responses[-1].date:%Y-%m-%d}"
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive)

docs.title: build_module
docs.text:
"""Create a subject, a module and its exercises from a plain Python outline.

Writes to the server. Everything it creates is deleted again at the end unless
you pass --keep.

Run:  pyhive examples run build_module PROGRAM_ID [--keep]
"""

import random
import string

from pyhive import HiveClient

OUTLINE = {
    "Python Basics": [
        "Variables and types",
        "Conditionals",
        "Loops",
        "Functions",
    ],
}


def main(client: HiveClient, *args: str) -> None:
    if not args:
        print("Pass a program id, e.g.: pyhive examples run build_module 2")
        return
    program = client.get_program(int(args[0]))
    keep = "--keep" in args

    symbol = "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_uppercase, k=2))
    subject = program.create_subject(
        symbol=symbol, name="PyHive example", color="#3F51B5"
    )
    print(f"Created subject [{subject.symbol}] {subject.name} (#{subject.id})")
    try:
        for order, (module_name, exercise_names) in enumerate(OUTLINE.items(), 1):
            module = subject.create_module(name=module_name, order=order)
            print(f"  module {module.name} (#{module.id})")
            for ex_order, exercise_name in enumerate(exercise_names, 1):
                exercise = module.create_exercise(
                    name=exercise_name, order=ex_order, expected_duration="45:00"
                )
                print(f"    exercise {exercise.name} (#{exercise.id})")
    finally:
        if not keep:
            # Deleting a subject deletes its modules and exercises with it.
            subject.delete()
            print("Deleted everything again (pass --keep to keep it).")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org", verify=False) as hive:
        main(hive, *sys.argv[1:])

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
pyhive is a synchronous Python client for the Hive LMS API. One object, HiveClient, signs in and exposes every resource as methods. Results come back as typed Pydantic models with helpers for walking between related objects.

from pyhive import HiveClient

with HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org") as client:
    for program in client.get_programs():
        for subject in program.get_subjects():
            print(program.name, subject.symbol, subject.name)

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install PyHiveLMS --index-url https://system-b90.github.io/.github/pypi/

To skip --index-url from now on: pip config set global.extra-index-url https://system-b90.github.io/.github/pypi/. In a requirements.txt, put --extra-index-url https://system-b90.github.io/.github/pypi/ above PyHiveLMS. Python 3.10 or newer.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
from pyhive import HiveClient

# Browser sign-in (SSO). The token refreshes itself.
client = HiveClient.from_sso("https://hive.org")

# Username and password. The token refreshes itself.
client = HiveClient("username", "password", "https://hive.org")

# A personal access token (hive_pat_...), made in Hive from the account
# menu, Access Tokens. Never refreshed: it works until it expires or is revoked.
client = HiveClient.from_access_token("hive_pat_...", "https://hive.org")

# An access token you already have (e.g. from `pyhive token`).
# It cannot refresh: when it expires, create a new client.
# A hive_pat_ token passed here is handled like from_access_token.
client = HiveClient.from_api_token(token, "https://hive.org")

# An access token plus its refresh token: refreshes itself.
client = HiveClient.from_api_token(
    token, "https://hive.org", refresh_token=refresh, auth_strategy="sso"
)

# Whatever the `pyhive` CLI would use: the server and sign-in cached by
# `pyhive auth login`, or -u/-p, HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN, then SSO.
from pyhive.cli.client_factory import default_hive_url, get_hive_client
client = get_hive_client(default_hive_url(), verify=False)

Use the client as a context manager (with ... as client:) to close its HTTP connection when you are done.

Every constructor also takes:

Keyword Default Meaning verify True Verify TLS. Pass False for a server with a self-signed certificate. timeout httpx's Seconds (float) or an httpx.Timeout. skip_version_check False Don't check the server's Hive version on connect (see Versions). headers, proxy Passed to the underlying httpx.Client.

Requests that get HTTP 502 are retried with backoff (up to 5 tries). A 401 triggers one token refresh and a retry, when the sign-in method can refresh.

docs.title: Personal access tokens
docs.text:
Segel and admins create personal access tokens in Hive (account menu, Access Tokens; admins can make them for any user). Each has a name, an expiry date (or none) and either read-only or read-and-write access. They are the simplest way to give a script or CI job its own credentials:

import os
from pyhive import HiveClient

client = HiveClient.from_access_token(os.environ["HIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN"], "https://hive.org")
  • from_access_token checks the token's format and checksum offline and raises ValueError for a mistyped or truncated one, before any request.
  • A token that Hive rejects raises AccessTokenRejectedError (a RuntimeError) carrying Hive's reason; it is never refreshed. An expired one raises its subclass AccessTokenExpiredError, whose message names the token and when it expired.
  • A read-only token used for a write raises AccessTokenReadOnlyError (a subclass of httpx.HTTPStatusError, status 403), whose message names the token and the refused method.
  • All three live in pyhive.src.access_tokens.

from pyhive.src.access_tokens import AccessTokenExpiredError, AccessTokenReadOnlyError

try:
    client.create_tag("urgent", "#ff0000")
except AccessTokenReadOnlyError:
    print("this token is read only")
except AccessTokenExpiredError as exc:
    print(exc)  # Access token "CI runner" expired on 2026-03-01 14:30 IST. Regenerate it ...
- Tokens can't be used to create, regenerate or revoke tokens; do that in Hive.

docs.title: Lists are generators
docs.text:
Every get_<things>() method returns a generator that pages through Hive as you iterate. Wrap it in list() to count, index or iterate twice.

subjects = list(client.get_subjects())
print(len(subjects), subjects[0].name)

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
List methods take keyword filters named after Hive's query parameters. Pass either ids or model objects wherever a related object is expected:

client.get_subjects(parent_program=program)            # or parent_program=2
client.get_modules(parent_subject__id=12)
client.get_exercises(parent_module=module)
client.get_assignments(for_user=student)               # or for_user=13
client.get_assignments(for_mentees_of=mentor, parent_subject=subject)
client.get_users(classes__id__in=[3, 4], clearance__in=[ClearanceEnum.HANICH])
client.get_classes(type_=ClassTypeEnum.ROOM)
client.get_help_requests(help_status__in=["Open"], ordering="-id")
  • subject_name=, module_name=, exercise_name=, program_name= match the name exactly.
  • Filters that contradict each other (for_user= and a different user__id__in=) raise AssertionError.

docs.title: One object
docs.text:
program = client.get_program(2)
subject = client.get_subject(12)
module = subject.get_module("Loops")      # by exact name; ValueError if 0 or 2+ match
exercise = module.get_exercise("For loops")
student = client.get_student(number=1234) # or name="First Last"

get_student returns None when no single student matches. get_user_by_name(name, clearance=...) does the same lookup for any user.

docs.title: Related objects
docs.text:
Models load related objects on first access and cache them:

assignment = client.get_assignment(1234)
assignment.user.display_name         # one request
assignment.exercise.parent_module    # one request each
student.mentor, student.classes, student.program

Each first access is a request. Inside a loop over hundreds of objects, fetch the related table once and join by id instead:

users = {user.id: user for user in client.get_users()}
for assignment in client.get_assignments():
    print(users[assignment.user_id].display_name, assignment.assignment_status.value)

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Models live in pyhive.types and are Pydantic V2 models:

from pyhive.types import Assignment, AssignmentStatusEnum, ClearanceEnum, Subject, User
  • Fields use Python names: related objects are ids named <thing>_id or <thing>_ids (user.mentor_id, user.class_ids, module.parent_subject_id).
  • model.to_dict() gives Hive's wire format ({"mentor": 1, "classes": [...]}), the same shape pyhive --json prints.
  • Enum fields hold enum members. Compare with members: assignment.assignment_status == AssignmentStatusEnum.DONE; use .value for the display string.
Model Helpers Program get_subjects(), create_subject(...), delete(), .checker, .default_class Subject get_modules(), get_module(name), create_module(...), delete(), .parent_program Module get_exercises(), get_exercise(name), create_exercise(...), delete(), .parent_subject Exercise get_assignments(), save(), notify_students(), delete(), .parent_module, .parent_subject Assignment get_responses(), .user, .checker, .exercise AssignmentResponse iter_contents(), .user, .assignment User get_assignments(), update(), set_queue(q), set_queues(...), delete(), .mentor, .mentees, .classes, .program, .queue, .user_queue, .override_queue, .current_assignment Class update(), delete(), set_queue(q), set_lesson(l), .users, .program Lesson get_rules(), .module Queue get_items(), add_item(...), update(...), duplicate(name), delete(), .user, .module, .subject, .program QueueItem update(...), move(n), expand(), delete(), .exercise, .nested_queue, .order, .queue_rule Help delete(), .user, .checker, .for_exercise

Common enums: ClearanceEnum (HANICH = student, CHECKER, SEGEL = staff, ADMIN), AssignmentStatusEnum (NEW, WORK_IN_PROGRESS, REDO, SUBMITTED, AUTOCHECKED, DONE), StatusEnum (where a student is: PRESENT, TOILET, HOME, …), GenderEnum, ClassTypeEnum (ROOM, STUDENT_GROUP), HelpTypeEnum, HelpStatusEnum, VisibilityEnum.

docs.title: Course content
docs.text:
program = client.get_program(2)
subject = program.create_subject(symbol="PY", name="Python", color="#3F51B5")
module = subject.create_module(name="Basics", order=1)
exercise = module.create_exercise(name="Loops", order=1, expected_duration="45:00")

exercise.on_creation_data = "loops_v2"
exercise.save()      # PUTs the writable fields, then refreshes from the reply

subject.delete()     # also deletes its modules and exercises

The same calls exist on the client: client.create_subject(symbol, name, program, color), client.create_module(name, parent_subject, order), client.create_exercise(name, order, parent_module, ...).

docs.title: Users and classes
docs.text:
from pyhive.types import ClassTypeEnum, ClearanceEnum, GenderEnum, StatusEnum

student = client.create_student(
    "jdoe", "S3cret!", GenderEnum.FEMALE, number=1234, program=2,
    first_name="Jane", last_name="Doe", mentor=mentor,
)
staff = client.create_user(
    "mentor1", "S3cret!", clearance=ClearanceEnum.SEGEL, gender=GenderEnum.MALE
)

student.status = StatusEnum.HOME     # change fields locally...
student.update()                     # ...then save them

group = client.create_class(
    "Group A", program=2, users=[student], type_=ClassTypeEnum.STUDENT_GROUP
)
client.get_students(of_class=group)  # also of_mentor=, of_program=

docs.title: Queues
docs.text:
A queue is the ordered list of exercises a student works through. It belongs to exactly one owner: a module (a module queue, shared) or a user (that user's own queue). Its items are exercises, other queues nested inside it, or a module's exercises.

from pyhive.types import QueueRuleEnum

queue = client.create_queue("Week 3", module=module)       # or user=student
queue.add_item(exercise=exercise)                            # appended
item = queue.add_item(nested_queue=other, queue_rule=QueueRuleEnum.WAIT_FOR_DONE)
item.move(0)                                 # 0-based; the rest are renumbered
item.update(enabled=False)                   # rule and flags; None = unchanged
item.expand()                                # replace it with the nested queue's items
copy = queue.duplicate("Week 3 (copy)")      # same owner, same items
queue.update(name="Week 3a")

Every student has three queue slots: queue (the class queue, usually set for a whole class), user_queue (their own queue) and override_queue. None clears a slot; a slot you leave out keeps its value:

client.set_user_queues(student, user_queue=own, disable_user_queue=False)
client.set_user_queues(student, override_queue=None)

group.set_queue(queue)        # every student in the class; None clears it
group.set_lesson(lesson)      # apply the lesson's queue rules to the class
client.unassign_class_override_queues(group)

Hive's own rules, which it enforces with a ValueError (HTTP 400): a user's own queue cannot be nested in a module queue or used in a lesson rule; an empty queue cannot be duplicated, and an empty module cannot be added as an item; an item's position changes only through move. Setting a class's lesson to None keeps the queues the lesson assigned.

docs.title: Assignments
docs.text:
client.patch_assignment(assignment, description="Look at line 12")
client.lock_assignment(assignment)       # the student can no longer submit
client.unlock_assignment(assignment)
for response in assignment.get_responses():
    print(response.date, response.response_type, response.dear_student)

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

start = datetime(2026, 11, 1, 8, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
event = client.create_schedule_event(start, start + timedelta(hours=2), title="Lecture")
client.create_event_attendee(event, attendee_class=3)    # a class attends
client.create_event_instructor(event, instructor=1)      # a user teaches

week = client.get_schedule_events(start__gte=start, end__lte=start + timedelta(days=7))
client.delete_schedule_event(event)

Newer Hive releases identify lessons, events, event categories, tags and their links by UUID instead of an integer. Methods that take one accept a UUID, its string form, an int, or the model itself.

docs.title: Help requests
docs.text:
chat = client.create_chat(with_user=student, title="Checking in")
for response in client.get_help_responses(chat):
    print(response.date, response.response_type)
chat.delete()

A staff account can open only chats. create_help_request with another HelpTypeEnum is for student accounts.

docs.title: Errors
Versions
docs.text:
When it connects, the client asks the server for its Hive version and checks it against the exact releases this PyHive is verified against (pyhive versions lists them). An unlisted release raises UnverifiedHiveVersionError: upgrade PyHive, or pass skip_version_check=True to try anyway.

client.get_hive_version()     # e.g. "7.2.0"

List help requests and chats get_help_request(help_id) One help request create_help_request(user, title, type_, exercise, visibility) Open a help request (student accounts) create_chat(with_user=, title=, about_exercise=, visibility=) Open a chat with a user delete_help_request(help_request), delete_chat(chat) Delete one get_help_responses(help), get_help_response(help, response_id) Replies on a help request get_help_response_student_file(help, response_id) The file attached to a reply, as bytes, or None get_notifications(was_read=, assignment=, help=, ...) List notifications get_notification(notification_id) One notification create_notification(user, help=, assignment=, comment=) Create a notification update_notification(notification, was_read=) Mark read / unread delete_notification(notification_id) Delete a notification

docs.title: Schedule and lessons
docs.text: Method Does get_schedule_events(start__gte=, end__lte=, lesson__id=) Events in a time window get_schedule_event(event_id) One event create_schedule_event(start, end, title=, category=, room=, lesson=, ...) Create an event delete_schedule_event(event_id) Delete an event get_event_categories(), get_event_category(id) Event categories create_event_category(name, color, ...), update_event_category(category, **fields), delete_event_category(id) Manage categories get_event_tags(), get_event_tag(id) Event tags create_event_tag(name, color), update_event_tag(id, name=, color=), delete_event_tag(id) Manage event tags get_event_taggings(), create_event_tagging(event, tag), delete_event_tagging(id) Tags on events get_event_attendees(), create_event_attendee(event, attendee_class), delete_event_attendee(id) Classes attending events get_event_instructors(), create_event_instructor(event, instructor), delete_event_instructor(id) Users teaching events get_lessons(module=), get_lesson(lesson_id) Lessons create_lesson(name, module, description=), update_lesson(lesson, **fields), delete_lesson(lesson_id) Manage lessons get_lesson_rules(lesson=) A lesson's queue rules create_lesson_rule(lesson=, ...), update_lesson_rule(lesson=, rule_id=, **fields), delete_lesson_rule(lesson=, rule_id=) Manage queue rules
